description: Structured eval definitions for the Neptune DB Cluster Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across workload types (production Multi-AZ Gremlin, dev single-instance, bulk load from S3, Neptune Analytics boundary redirect, missing prerequisites). Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: Production Neptune DB Multi-AZ with CMK + TLS + IAM auth + Streams
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — all checklist items verified, Multi-AZ reader promotion + customer CMK + neptune_enforce_ssl + IAM database auth + Streams + snapshots
eval_cases.prompt: Provision a production Amazon Neptune DB cluster named "prod-graph" in us-east-1 for a Gremlin property-graph workload. We need 1 writer + 2 readers across 3 AZs for Multi-AZ failover. Use db.r6g.8xlarge instances. Engine version 1.3.2.0. The graph is ~200M vertices + 1B edges. Customer-managed CMK alias/prod-graph-kms for encryption at rest. Enable TLS (neptune_enforce_ssl=1) and IAM database auth. Set neptune_query_timeout=30000 (OLTP queries). Enable Neptune Streams for change capture. Snapshots: 7-day retention. Deletion protection enabled. Subnet group prod-neptune-subnet spans 3 AZs. Security group sg-neptune123 inbound 8182 from sg-app456. Tags: Environment=production, Workload=graph. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
NEPTUNE: prod-graph
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Service: Neptune DB (NOT Analytics)
  [✓] Engine version: 1.3.2.0 (pinned)
  [✓] Writer instance: db.r6g.8xlarge
  [✓] Reader instances: 2 (across us-east-1b, us-east-1c for Multi-AZ)
  [✓] Multi-AZ with reader promotion: Enabled
  [✓] Subnet group: prod-neptune-subnet (3 AZs)
  [✓] Security group: sg-neptune123 (inbound 8182 from sg-app456)
  [✓] Encryption at rest: Enabled (customer CMK alias/prod-graph-kms)
  [✓] TLS / neptune_enforce_ssl: Enabled
  [✓] IAM database auth: Enabled
  [✓] Parameter group: neptune_query_timeout=30000, neptune_streams=1
  [✓] Snapshot retention: 7 days
  [✓] Deletion protection: Enabled
  [✓] Query languages: Gremlin
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws neptune describe-db-clusters --db-cluster-identifier prod-graph
  aws neptune describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier prod-graph-instance-1
  aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/prod-graph-kms

eval_cases.name: Dev Neptune DB single writer instance (no Multi-AZ)
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — dev cluster with single writer; explicit 'NO failover' notation; AWS-managed KMS; neptune_enforce_ssl=1 hygiene
eval_cases.prompt: Provision a dev Neptune DB cluster named "dev-graph" in us-east-1. Just a single writer instance for functional testing — no Multi-AZ, no failover needed. Use db.r6g.large. Engine version 1.3.2.0. Enable neptune_enforce_ssl=1 for good hygiene. AWS-managed KMS key is fine (no customer CMK). Subnet group dev-neptune-subnet in one AZ is OK for dev. Security group sg-dev-neptune inbound 8182 from sg-dev-app. Tags: Environment=dev, Workload=graph. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
NEPTUNE: dev-graph
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Service: Neptune DB (NOT Analytics)
  [✓] Engine version: 1.3.2.0 (pinned)
  [✓] Writer instance: db.r6g.large
  [✓] Reader instances: 0 (writer-only — NO failover)
  [✓] Multi-AZ with reader promotion: Disabled (writer-only — NO failover)
  [✓] Subnet group: dev-neptune-subnet
  [✓] Security group: sg-dev-neptune (inbound 8182 from sg-dev-app)
  [✓] Encryption at rest: Enabled (AWS-managed)
  [✓] TLS / neptune_enforce_ssl: Enabled
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws neptune describe-db-clusters --db-cluster-identifier dev-graph

eval_cases.name: Neptune DB with initial Gremlin data bulk load from S3
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — Multi-AZ cluster with bulk load source cited (same-region S3 bucket, IAM role NeptuneLoadRole); loader prerequisites verified
eval_cases.prompt: Provision a Neptune DB cluster named "analytics-graph" in us-east-1 for a Gremlin property-graph workload. 1 writer + 1 reader for Multi-AZ, db.r6g.4xlarge. Engine version 1.3.2.0. Customer CMK alias/graph-kms. neptune_enforce_ssl=1, IAM database auth. Snapshots 7 days. Deletion protection enabled. We need to load initial data from s3://graph-data-bucket/v1/ (same region us-east-1) using IAM role NeptuneLoadRole. Subnet group graph-subnet spans 2 AZs. Security group sg-graph inbound 8182 from sg-graph-app. Tags: Environment=production, Workload=graph-bulk-load. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
NEPTUNE: analytics-graph
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Service: Neptune DB (NOT Analytics)
  [✓] Writer instance: db.r6g.4xlarge
  [✓] Reader instances: 1 (Multi-AZ)
  [✓] Multi-AZ with reader promotion: Enabled
  [✓] Subnet group: graph-subnet (2 AZs)
  [✓] Security group: sg-graph (inbound 8182 from sg-graph-app)
  [✓] Encryption at rest: Enabled (customer CMK alias/graph-kms)
  [✓] TLS / neptune_enforce_ssl: Enabled
  [✓] IAM database auth: Enabled
  [✓] Snapshot retention: 7 days
  [✓] Deletion protection: Enabled
  [✓] Bulk load source: s3://graph-data-bucket/v1/ (same region, IAM role NeptuneLoadRole)
  [✓] Query languages: Gremlin
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws neptune describe-db-clusters --db-cluster-identifier analytics-graph
  aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/graph-kms

eval_cases.name: Operator requests PageRank — redirect to Neptune Analytics
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — workload is analytical (PageRank, connected-components on a large graph); Neptune DB is the wrong service; redirect to Neptune Analytics (separate aws graph API)
eval_cases.prompt: I need to run PageRank and connected-components on a 500M-vertex graph in AWS. Provision a Neptune cluster named "research-graph" in us-east-1 with db.x2gdb.16xlarge instances for this. We want Multi-AZ and snapshots. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
NEPTUNE: research-graph
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Service: workload is analytical (PageRank, connected-components on a large graph) — Neptune DB has NO built-in algorithm library; redirect to Neptune Analytics (separate aws graph API)
  [✗] Topology mismatch: Neptune Analytics uses a single graph (no writer/reader split, no Multi-AZ failover); the requested Multi-AZ does not apply
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws graph list-graphs  # Neptune Analytics API (separate from aws neptune)

eval_cases.name: Operator has not specified subnet group, security group, or CMK
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — subnet group (Multi-AZ requires multi-AZ subnet group), security group (port 8182 inbound), and customer CMK ARN all unspecified
eval_cases.prompt: Help me create a new Neptune DB cluster called "user-graph" in us-east-1. I want Multi-AZ failover and a customer-managed CMK for encryption. We will store user-relationship data. Region: us-east-1, Account: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
NEPTUNE: user-graph
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Subnet group: NOT specified — Multi-AZ requires subnet group spanning >=2 AZs
  [✗] Security group: NOT specified — Neptune needs inbound 8182 from application SG
  [✗] KMS key: NOT specified — customer-managed CMK requires a key ARN in the same region
  [✗] Instance class / workload size: NOT specified — drives writer/reader sizing
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws ec2 describe-subnets --query 'Subnets[*].AvailabilityZone' --output text
  aws ec2 describe-security-groups --query 'SecurityGroups[*].[GroupId,GroupName]' --output text
  aws kms list-aliases --query 'Aliases[?starts_with(AliasName, `alias/`)]'
